quotes.note: Participating narrator uses “my” and “I” in retrospective narration about his relationship with a woman.
Story-world exposition contains no narrator-participation marker and is compatible with either first- or third-person narration.
Participating narrator recounts his own decision using repeated narratorial “I.”
Brief setting exposition identifies no narrating person.
Gnomic universal “your” is generic address, not sustained second-person narration of a protagonist.
Direct-address question is dialogue and does not identify the base narrator.
Narratorial “I noted” reports the participating narrator’s perception of a specific answer.
Although clipped, “reminding myself” exposes the participating narrator during a story-specific moment.
Universal reflection about everybody and somebody is gnomic rather than diagnostic base narration.
Severe truncation removes the clause boundaries and narrator context needed for person attribution.
Aphoristic statement about ruleless institutions is gnomic and may also be clipped from speech.
Gnomic fragment has no narrator or finite narrative clause.
The dialogue itself is nondiagnostic, but the external speech tag “I said” exposes first-person base narration.
Sustained external narration follows an antagonist as “he,” reports his observation and concern, and is not framed by a participating narrator.
General explanatory statement about the DRD4 gene is gnomic and potentially spoken.
The truncated mixture of definition and story fragment lacks recoverable quotation and narration boundaries.

person_note: The book alternates sustained narrative persons: Jack McEvoy narrates the principal investigation as a participating first-person narrator, while autonomous antagonist sections use third-person narration for Hammond and the Shrike. The Goodreads evidence independently contains both unmistakable first-person base narration and a sustained third-person Hammond scene, matching the authorized opening and several Tier C whole-book structural descriptions. Gnomic “you,” dialogue, and clipped fragments do not create additional narrative persons. Confidence is medium because the authorized prose excerpt covers only the first-person opening and the whole-book structural sources are Tier C.
